extracted.intended_audience: persons/applicants filing international design (Hague) applications through the USPTO via EFS-Web (registered and unregistered eFilers)
extracted.subtask_short: filing Hague design via USPTO EFS-Web
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step quick start procedural guide for submitting an International Design Application (Hague) through the USPTO using the EFS‑Web electronic filing system, covering eligibility, data entry, document attachments, fee calculation, payment, saving, and follow-on submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to file through USPTO as office of indirect filing
rubrics_metrics.description: To file an international design application through the USPTO as an office of indirect filing, the applicant, or each applicant if there is more than one applicant, must be a national of the United States or have a domicile, a habitual residence, or a real and effective industrial or commercial establishment in the United States. In addition, the applicant, or each applicant if there is more than one applicant, must indicate the United States as their Contracting Party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement should appear in the appropriate sections of the DM/1 Form. Warning repeated elsewhere: To file through USPTO as office of indirect filing, each applicant must meet the U.S. nationality/residence/establishment criteria and indicate the United States as their Contracting Party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Must access and select correct EFS‑Web filing type
rubrics_metrics.description: You must be able to access EFS-Web. The radio button 'International Design Application (Hague) for filing through the USPTO as an Office of indirect filing' must be selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting a new application choose 'New application/Proceeding' then select the radio button next to the Hague filing option before continuing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered vs Unregistered eFiler capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: You can be either a Registered or Unregistered eFiler. Only Registered eFilers may: save a submission as a work-in-progress for up to 7 days; submit follow-on documents and/or fees into an existing Hague filing via the Electronic Filing System; view an international design application in Private PAIR upon association of the Registered eFiler’s digital certificate with a customer number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered eFilers must certify they are the certificate holder or working under authority of the certificate holder when signing on.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFS‑Web session timeout
rubrics_metrics.description: EFS-Web sessions will time-out after one hour of inactivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Hague submission that has not been submitted or saved after one hour of inactivity will be lost. You will need to login again and re-enter the information from the start.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing-on as Registered eFiler
rubrics_metrics.description: Once you have signed-on to EFS-Web as a Registered eFiler, you will need to certify that you are the certificate holder or working under the authority of the certificate holder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered eFilers who authenticate can save in-progress submissions and return to edit prior to completing the submission, but any required payment will be due upon filing of the completed submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing-on as Unregistered eFiler
rubrics_metrics.description: Once you have signed-on to EFS-Web as an Unregistered eFiler, you will need to enter your last name, first name and e-mail address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process for starting a 'New application/Proceeding' is the same: select the Hague radio button and click Continue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Data page sections required
rubrics_metrics.description: On the 'Application Data' page, the following sections shall be available for completion: Application Data; Applicant Name (Natural Person or Legal Entity); Correspondence Address (Customer Number or Correspondence Address).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you complete the appropriate subsection fields for the applicant type and correspondence choice before continuing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of invention optional and length/character limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of the invention may be provided but is not required. If provided, the title of the invention may not exceed 500 characters in length and must be as short and specific as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters that cannot be captured in the Office’s automated systems may not be reflected in records. If the United States is designated, a title furnished via EFS-Web may be used as the title in USPTO communications. View list of valid characters for a patent title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney Docket Number format
rubrics_metrics.description: An Attorney Docket Number is a Reference text of up to 25 alphanumeric characters that is used to identify a patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This number is not assigned by the USPTO and can be any combination of numbers and letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant name formatting for natural persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Names of natural persons shall be indicated by the person's family name and given name(s), the family name being indicated before the given name(s). When the Natural Person radio button is selected the First name and Last name fields must be completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the exact ordering (family name before given names) when entering natural person applicant names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant name formatting for legal entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Names of legal entities shall be indicated by their full, official designations. When the Legal Entity radio button is selected the Name field must be completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the entity's full official designation exactly as intended for recordation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address options and required fields
rubrics_metrics.description: The correspondence address may be indicated by a customer number or by entering a correspondence address. If the Customer Number radio button is selected, the user may select their customer number from the dropdown or manually enter the number. If the Correspondence Address radio button is selected, the user must complete Name 1, Street Address 1, City, Country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a customer number is not entered, the submitted application will not be associated with the Registered eFiler’s digital certificate and will not be viewable in Private PAIR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer number not to be used in DM/1 address fields
rubrics_metrics.description: A customer number should not be used to specify a correspondence address in the 'Application for International Registration' (DM/1 form), as the address fields in the DM/1 form are for use by the International Bureau, which does not recognize customer numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead, furnish the customer number in a separate signed document (e.g., a transmittal letter) that accompanies the DM/1 form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attach Documents: two sections
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Attach Documents' screen has two different sections for attaching documents: (1) 'Attach Documents other than Reproductions' and (2) 'Attach Reproductions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate section depending on whether the file is a reproduction (drawing/photo) or other document (DM/1, annexes, transmittal letters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include DM/1 form (or equivalent)
rubrics_metrics.description: New international design applications filed through the USPTO should always include the DM/1 form (or a form having the same format and contents as the DM/1 form).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The DM/1 form includes boxes for applicant, entitlement, Contracting Party, creator, designations, and other relevant information. Use document description 'App for Intl Registration (DM/1 or equiv)' when attaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annexes to DM/1 and their document descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any annexes to the DM/1 form should be attached in EFS-Web using the document description 'Annex(es) to the DM/1 or equivalent'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annexes relevant to U.S. designation include inventor's oath/declaration, micro entity certification, and an information disclosure statement (IDS). Note: IDS may be submitted directly to the USPTO after WIPO publication and will be considered if filed within three months from publication or per 37 CFR 1.97.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for attaching non-reproduction documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 1: Click 'Browse/Choose File' to search your computer for the document. Step 2: After upload, index it correctly using the 'Category' and 'Document Description' dropdown menus. Add additional documents by clicking 'Add File' and repeating steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use representative file names; ensure proper indexing so documents are correctly identified upon submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproductions technical and format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproductions may be drawings, photographs, or a combination and may be black and white or color. Technical requirements (resolution, min/max size, border width) are set forth on WIPO website. Reproductions should be submitted as single page PDF or JPEG files via the 'Attach Reproductions' section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the 'Attach Reproductions' section is strongly recommended to avoid incurring additional per-page publication fees that might be required if treated as paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproductions file size and content rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Each single page PDF or JPEG file attached through 'Attach Reproductions' cannot exceed a file size of two megabytes. Each image file should contain only one view of the design and should not include any numbering of the reproduction in the image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproduction numbering is accomplished by the 'Attach Reproductions' section which prompts input of a design and view number for each file.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFS‑Web validation behavior for JPEG and PDF reproductions
rubrics_metrics.description: For JPEG submissions, EFS-Web will provide warnings where requirements pertaining to image resolution and minimum and maximum dimensions have not been satisfied; EFS-Web does not check color mode or border size for JPEG images. For PDF submissions via 'Attach Reproductions', EFS-Web will not permit submission of any PDF file that is more than one page; EFS-Web does not check color mode, border size, resolution, or maximum or minimum dimensions of the reproduction (other than certain minimum and maximum page size dimensions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate document description ('drawings – only black and white line drawings' or 'drawing – other than black and white line drawings') when attaching reproductions. EFS-Web will warn if submission lacks an indication that at least one reproduction is attached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for attaching reproductions (indexing and types)
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 1: Click 'Browse/Choose File' to locate the JPEG or PDF. Step 2: After upload, index it correctly. In 'Attach Reproductions' the 'Category' dropdown is not available; use 'Document Description' to indicate whether the drawing is Black and White or Other than Black and White.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add additional views with 'Add View' and additional designs with 'Add Design'; repeat upload/index steps for each view. Use 'Upload & Validate' after all documents uploaded. Move views with 'Move Down'/'Move Up'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Documents validation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: On the 'Review Documents' screen, confirm that all necessary documents uploaded properly. If you receive any validation errors you will not be able to proceed to the next screen until the errors are fixed. You will be able to proceed if you receive any validation warnings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a document could not be validated, an error message will inform you of the reason (e.g., attaching a document that is not PDF or JPEG will cause validation failure, as will not choosing a document description).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal fee and USPTO transmission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An international design application filed with the USPTO as an office of indirect filing is subject to payment of a transmittal fee to the USPTO, in addition to the applicable international fees payable to the International Bureau. The USPTO will not transmit the international design application to the International Bureau if the transmittal fee has not been paid to the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the current USPTO fee schedule for the correct transmittal fee amount. Certain international fees payable to the International Bureau may be paid through USPTO only if paid no later than the transmittal fee payment date; payments through USPTO must be in U.S. dollars and currency conversion may result in additional amounts owed to WIPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: WIPO international fees and use of WIPO Fee Calculator
rubrics_metrics.description: International fees payable to WIPO include the basic fee, designation fee(s), publication fee, and a fee for a description exceeding 100 words. The 'Calculate Fees' screen of EFS-Web provides for input of one lump sum in Swiss francs and includes a link to the WIPO Hague System Fee Calculator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the WIPO Fee Calculator to determine total CHF amount, then copy/paste into the EFS-Web field; EFS-Web will calculate the USD amount based on current exchange rates. EFS-Web only permits payment of international fees through USPTO until midnight ET of the date of payment of the transmittal fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity status selection and discounts for transmittal fee
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Calculate Fees' screen allows eFilers to select the appropriate entity status. Effective January 16, 2018, a small entity discount of 50% and a micro entity discount of 75% are available with respect to the transmittal fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions for qualifying for small or micro entity status are set forth in 37 CFR 1.27 and 1.29; to establish micro entity status submit Form PTO/SB/15A or PTO/SB/15B; small entity may be established by a signed written assertion of entitlement (37 CFR 1.27(c)(1)). Box 18 of the DM/1 form may be used to provide the assertion for U.S. designation. Selecting entity status on EFS-Web does not change WIPO-calculated CHF fees; WIPO Fee Calculator should already account for any U.S. designation reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirm & Submit: final review and single-submit instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: On the 'Confirm & Submit' screen you will be presented with a review of the content provided for the international design application submission including Application Data, fees, and uploaded documents. Ensure Bibliographic Data is correct; all documents have been attached; then click on the 'Submit' button once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click Submit only once; incomplete reviews or missing attachments may cause errors. Registered eFilers can also 'Save for Later Submission' if conditions are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay Fees: payment methods and flow
rubrics_metrics.description: On the 'Pay Fees' screen you have the option of paying via 'USPTO Deposit Account,' 'Credit/Debit Card,' or 'Electronic Funds Transfer.' To make a payment click 'Pay with the New USPTO Payment System' to be directed to Financial Manager.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once on Financial Manager you may pay as Guest with Credit/Debit Card or sign in to use stored payment methods. You cannot view the 'Pay Fees' screen if fees were not previously calculated; you will be forwarded to the 'Receipt' screen instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement Receipt contents and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Once payment is processed successfully, you will receive your Acknowledgement Receipt on the 'Receipt' screen. Registered eFilers will also have the option of viewing the Acknowledgement Receipt under 'My Workplace' on EFS-Web.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Acknowledgement Receipt displays details of the submission: file names of uploaded documents and reproduction files, time stamp, and total amount paid. You may print or save the receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Save Submission feature for Registered eFilers
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered eFilers may save a submission for later; you must complete all required fields on the 'Application Data' screen and attach at least one document on the 'Attach Documents' screen to save the submission. The submission may be saved for up to 7 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When saving, warnings will appear (e.g., fees calculated may not be accurate later), and the saved package must be retrieved by logging into EFS-Web as a Registered eFiler via My Workplace > Saved Submission Package > My Saved Packages. The submission is not filed officially until the Submit function is executed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-on submissions limitations and routing
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered eFilers may file follow-on submissions in international design applications through EFS-Web. However, the USPTO will not forward to the International Bureau follow-on submissions that are received after an international design application has been transmitted to the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If International Bureau sends an invitation requiring compliance under the Hague Agreement, replies must be filed directly with the International Bureau to avoid abandonment or loss of rights. After transmittal, EFS-Web document descriptions and fees available differ and generally relate only to U.S. national processing/examination. No follow-on submission or fee payment is required to initiate U.S. examination upon WIPO publication. Reproductions amended pursuant to 37 CFR 1.121 may be submitted via EFS-Web as PDF or JPEG (JPEG must be attached using the 'Attach JPEG Reproductions' section).

rubrics_metrics.name: Six-month transmittal to WIPO filing date warning
rubrics_metrics.description: An international design application not received by the International Bureau within six months from the date the international design application is received by the USPTO will not be entitled to a filing date as of the date of receipt by the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure timely transmittal to WIPO; payment of the transmittal fee and correct processing are required so USPTO will transmit within required timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact support for EFS‑Web filing assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have any questions or concerns regarding filing in EFS-Web, contact the Patent EBC Monday - Friday, from 6:00 a.m. to 12 Midnight Eastern Time, by email ebc@uspto.gov or telephone 866-217-9197.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use support for technical or procedural help during filing, saving, payment, and follow-on submission processes.
